projects.name: Plants Vs Zombies
projects.desc: A Plants vs. Zombies style Windows tower-defense game in C++ with SFML: place plants, collect suns and stop zombie waves.
projects.long: Players place plants on a lawn to stop waves of zombies from reaching the house. Plants shoot automatically, sunflowers and falling suns supply the resources used to buy new plants, and zombies spawn on multiple rows with HP bars. The game runs on a classic loop of events, update and render, coordinated by PlantManager, ZombieManager, BulletManager, SunManager and a CollisionManager, with SFML handling graphics, audio, windowing and input. Controls are mouse-driven (click to collect suns, select and place plants, press Start in the menu). Ships as a Visual Studio solution for Windows with SFML runtime DLLs, plus an ASCII architecture diagram of the whole game loop.

projects.name: Masm Debugger Clone
projects.desc: A console MASM-style virtual machine and debugger in C++ for stepping through assembly and inspecting CPU state.
projects.long: A console-based virtual machine emulator inspired by vintage emulators, built to show how a processor handles tasks at a low level. It simulates a simplified CPU with customizable registers and flags, supports hex-dump memory views with editing, assembly input and execution, step-by-step tracing with real-time register updates, and debugging aids such as breakpoints and memory watches. A command shell (dump, enter, fill, move, search, assemble, unassemble, trace) drives it, and instructions persist to memory.txt. Designed for education and system-level debugging, and released under the MIT License.
